title: OSHA 300 Log Checklist (29 CFR 1904.29)
subtitle: Use when auditing injury and illness records and before completing the year's 300-A summary.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
For a Defect, correct the form or entry, note the date it was fixed, and recheck the item.
Company recordkeeping procedures and site rules may add checks; this list covers 1904.29 only.

sections.title: Forms in use
items: Log, summary and incident report forms (OSHA or equivalent) are used for every recordable case
Any substitute form holds the same information as the OSHA form, is as readable, and follows the same instructions
An insurance form used instead of the 301 carries every item the 301 asks for, with OSHA-required details added where missing
The recordkeeping system can print equivalent forms on request

sections.title: 300 Log, 300-A and 301 entries
items: Business information is filled in at the top of the current log
Every logged case has a short description of one or two lines
Last year's log totals are summarized on a 300-A
Each case number on the log has a matching 301 or equivalent incident report
Dates show each case was logged and its 301 completed no more than 7 calendar days after the information was received

sections.title: Privacy concern cases
items: Cases in every 1904.29(b)(7) category, such as mental illness or an injury from sexual assault, are handled as privacy cases
Contaminated needlesticks and sharps cuts of the kind described in 1904.29(b)(7)(v) are entered as privacy cases
Other illnesses are marked privacy case only where the employee voluntarily asked
No case outside the 1904.29(b)(7) list is recorded with a privacy case entry
The words "privacy case" stand in place of the name; no employee name appears for these entries
A separate confidential list links case numbers to employee names and is kept up to date
Where a description could still point to the worker, the log and incident report give the cause and general severity without intimate details

sections.title: Disclosure of the forms
items: Copies given to anyone outside the government, employees, former employees and authorized representatives had names and identifying details removed or hidden
Unredacted copies went only to an auditor or consultant the employer hired to evaluate the safety and health program
Names were shared only as far as needed to process a workers' compensation or other insurance benefits claim
Disclosures with names to a public health authority or law enforcement agency are limited to uses that need no consent, authorization or opportunity to agree or object under 45 CFR 164.512

references: 29 CFR 1904.29: Forms (Part 1904 Subpart C: Recordkeeping Forms and Recording Criteria)
